versions.changelog: v3.0.1: icon release — new skill icon in the family flat style (white ground, steel-blue frame, signal-yellow hatch, dual-page A-to-ZH translation motif), shipped as assets/icon-512.png. No code changes; all v3.0.0 capabilities included. 觉得有用的话，欢迎 Star（GitHub）或收藏（SkillHub 技能页）。

v3.0.0 major release. 1) Zero-dependency direct mode - no engine, no endpoint, no API key: extract line-level text from tier-A documents (fully offline), you/your model translate the JSON, apply refills translations into the PDF (images and vector graphics preserved, text stays selectable and searchable, --dual side-by-side layout). 2) One-command setup: writes your endpoint config (0600), validates connectivity (fail-closed), prints engine install guidance - the tool never installs packages itself. 3) All v2.10.0 capabilities included (glossary injection takes real effect, page-level low-confidence hotspots, batch wiring fixes). 195 offline tests, 30-check live battery, security hard-lines zero. Star the GitHub repo or bookmark the SkillHub page if you find it useful.

v2.10.0 - Terminology consistency & quality transparency. 1) Injected glossaries (built-in medical table, user CSV, adaptive seeding) now disable the engine's automatic term extraction - the engine's own extraction shadows injected tables when non-empty, and combined with injected tables it has real-world hang instances (6/6 reproduced live); injection now takes real effect. 2) Adaptive term seeding (experimental, opt-in via --seed-terms): extracts up to 12 high-frequency document terms, translates them via one small request to YOUR configured endpoint, merges with the built-in medical glossary; terms with empty or missing translations are never written into the glossary (known engine crasher). 3) Tier-C page-level quality hotspots: per-page OCR confidence aggregated; low-confidence pages listed in the audit, translate output and batch reports for targeted human review. 4) Batch fixes: encrypted-PDF --password wired (was a latent NameError), tier-C LLM proofread actually wired (the v2.9.0 claim is now real), --seed-terms / --no-ocr-proofread flags. 5) translate --auto-lang actually works now (was a dead flag). 6) Correction: the v2.9.0 changelog claimed a segment-level translation cache that did not exist - the dead module has been removed and the claim is corrected here. 168 offline tests, 22/22 real-network battery, security self-scan hard lines zero.

v2.6.0 - Translation efficiency and intelligence. 1) Segment-level translation cache: batch mode automatically checks a SQLite-backed cache (SHA256 keyed by source text + language pair + model) before calling the engine - reduces LLM calls by 30-50% for batch jobs with overlapping content. 2) Source language auto-detection: analyzes PDF sample pages across 9 languages (en/zh/ja/ko/fr/de/es/ru/pt) to set --lang-in automatically instead of defaulting to English (--auto-lang flag). 3) Batch path now includes OCR proofread (closes the v2.3.0 review P1 gap where proofread was translate-only). 4) Batch audit gained large_doc_policy section. 136 offline tests, real-network battery 18/18, security self-scan hard assertions passed.

v2.8.0 - Editable DOCX output and batch policy transparency. New: --output-format docx converts the translated PDF into an editable Word document via LibreOffice (for revisions, advisor comments, and journal submission systems). Batch audit trail now includes large_doc_policy section (partitioning and glossary-skip decisions are traceable). merge/split/estimate subcommands close the partitioned-translation loop. 130 offline tests, real-network battery 18/18, security self-scan hard assertions passed.

v2.7.0 - Document pipeline completion. New: merge subcommand (combines multiple PDFs), split subcommand (breaks by page-range expression), estimate subcommand (dry-run: pages/chars/parts/duration without touching any endpoint). XLSX/ODS input support via LibreOffice calc conversion. Estimate div-zero fix, corrupted-PDF exception handling, fake privacy line removal. 136 offline tests, real-network battery 18/18, security self-scan hard assertions passed.

v2.6.0 - Translation efficiency and intelligence. 1) Segment-level translation cache: batch mode automatically checks a SQLite-backed cache (SHA256 keyed by source text + language pair + model) before calling the engine - reduces LLM calls by 30-50% for batch jobs with overlapping content. 2) Source language auto-detection: analyzes PDF sample pages across 9 languages (en/zh/ja/ko/fr/de/es/ru/pt) to set --lang-in automatically instead of defaulting to English (--auto-lang flag). 3) Batch path now includes OCR proofread (closes the v2.3.0 review P1 gap where proofread was translate-only). 4) Batch audit gained large_doc_policy section. 136 offline tests, real-network battery 18/18, security self-scan hard assertions passed.

v2.5.0 - Editable DOCX output and batch policy transparency. New: --output-format docx converts the translated PDF into an editable Word document via LibreOffice (for revisions, advisor comments, and journal submission systems). Batch audit trail now includes large_doc_policy section (partitioning and glossary-skip decisions are traceable). merge/split/estimate subcommands close the partitioned-translation loop. 130 offline tests, real-network battery 18/18, security self-scan hard assertions passed.

v2.4.0 - Document pipeline completion: merge, split, and estimate subcommands. merge combines multiple PDFs into one (closes the --pages partitioned-translation loop). split breaks a PDF by page-range expression (each range becomes its own file, ready for --pages partitioned translation). estimate dry-runs a document: pages, character count, image pages, partition strategy, and estimated duration - zero endpoint calls. audit.jsonl gained large_doc_policy in the batch path. 130 offline tests, real-network battery 18/18, security self-scan hard assertions passed.

v2.3.0 - LLM proofreading for tier-C scans: after the OCR rebuilt text layer, line text is sent to YOUR configured endpoint for a fix-OCR-errors-only pass (truncation and line-count anomalies gracefully degrade to the original text; stats in the audit trail) - catching misrecognized characters before translation. Disable with --no-ocr-proofread. Security declaration updated: proofread traffic follows the same data boundary as translation (your endpoint only). Stale test scaffolding fixed. 123 offline tests; real-network battery green on the GLM path; pre-release security self-scan hard assertions passed.

v2.2.0 - Tier-C repair layer 2.0: drop-level noise lines (watermarks, ICP filings) are now removed from the rebuilt OCR text layer before translation, with per-line glue-splitting when wordninja is available; repair stats land in the audit trail. New: --glossaries-file for user-supplied terminology CSVs (repeatable, stacks on the built-in medical glossary). New: Word/PowerPoint input (.docx/.pptx/.ppt) via headless LibreOffice with actionable guidance when missing. 117 offline tests; battery 18/18 on the GLM path (multi-vendor leg skipped: third-party endpoint account balance).

Medical-terminology consistency and visual batch reporting. 1) A bundled 45-term medical EN-to-ZH glossary is injected into the engine's glossary pipeline by default (RCT, systematic review, confidence interval, hazard ratio, JIA, rituximab and more - forced consistent translations); disable with --no-medical-glossary, other language directions unaffected. 2) Batch mode now also produces a self-contained report.html: summary cards, A/B/C tier distribution, color-coded per-file status with failure reasons and large-document policy markers - single file, offline readable. 3) Other directions and disabled states have zero behavior change. 110 offline tests, real-network acceptance battery, pre-release security self-scan passed.

Major release: oversized-PDF reliability. 1) Large-document auto strategy: PDFs of 40+ pages are automatically partitioned (25 pages/part, engine-native splitting with automatic merge - isolated failures and per-part timeout budgets; --part-pages to tune, 0 disables) and glossary extraction is skipped automatically (root cure for the STTT review timeout case; --glossary auto|off). 2) Tier-C OCR pipeline rewritten: instead of tesseract's raw text layer, the line-frame TSV output is rebuilt into a repaired invisible text layer (control chars stripped, CJK pseudo-spaces removed - line-level repair now genuinely applies to the translation source), with automatic CJK font selection and failed-page image preservation. 3) Audit trail gained a large_doc_policy section (partitioning and glossary decisions are traceable). 107 offline tests, throttled real-network battery 18/18, pre-release security self-scan hard assertions passed.

Compatibility and transparency release: 1) fixed a single-line YAML pitfall in the SKILL.md description field (a colon followed by a space can make strict Agent-skill parsers reject the file as invalid); all channels now parse cleanly. 2) Added a Security & behavior declaration section: local-first operation (triage/detection/reports run locally), data boundary (PDF text goes only to your configured endpoint, keys never leave your machine), subprocess isolation, and write scope - making the trust story explicit and auditable. 3) Offline suite grown to 98 tests with YAML smoke and declaration anti-regression assertions. No behavior changes versus 1.2.0.

Timeout robustness for large documents (driven by real-world STTT review case): 1) fixed DOC_HOLMES_OPENAI_TIMEOUT never reaching the engine (HTTP timeout was stuck at 60s); 2) default per-request HTTP timeout raised 60s to 180s; 3) new --no-glossary flag skips the automatic term-extraction stage, which could stall on very large or text-dense PDFs (8000+ chars/page reviews); 4) troubleshooting docs gained a large-document timeout entry; 5) hardening wording pass. 94 offline tests plus a throttled real-network acceptance battery, and a pre-release security self-scan (12 pattern categories, hard assertions).

Tier-B upgrade, step one: span-level duplicate-layer detection (same-text near-overlap counting with samples into the audit trail; redaction surgery was tested and deliberately NOT shipped - removing either copy of overlapping glyphs destroys both, so detection replaces surgery on the conservative-side principle). V5 text-repair engine for audit statistics: CJK pseudo-space removal and glued-word splitting (camelCase boundaries with a medical-journal-abbreviation protection table, optional wordninja). Translation subprocess timeout now kills the whole process group (no orphaned grandchildren burning quota). BabelDOC underlying paper formally published at ACL 2026. 91 offline tests plus a real-network acceptance battery.

Endpoint-safety hotfix: no endpoint or credentials are bundled anymore - users configure their own OpenAI-compatible endpoint and API key (official Zhipu open platform free tier recommended). GLM Coding Plan subscription endpoints now require a one-time billing acknowledgment (per the official FAQ, plan quota only applies to designated coding tools; other calls are billed per-token against balance, and shared subscriptions face restrictions) via DOC_HOLMES_ALLOW_CODING_ENDPOINT=1. Default model for the official platform: glm-4.5-flash (free tier). All 75 offline tests green.

Initial release: layout-preserving PDF translation with automatic A/B/C triage (A clean born-digital = high fidelity; B noisy text layer = translated with a noise report; C scanned = experimental OCR channel whose output carries a preview-quality notice page). Bilingual side-by-side plus pure-translation outputs, batch mode with resume / per-file timeout / audit trail / rollback, pay-per-token endpoint guard, env-only configuration, MIT glue code over the BabelDOC engine (pdf2zh-next) invoked as a subprocess. 63 offline tests plus a real-network acceptance battery.
